trail.text: Flagged latencies point at route and travel — digging in to find the real source.
Many services are slow at once — checking shared backends for the common cause.
Timelines are nearly simultaneous — checking who moved first and looking for hidden resource strain.
All spikes hit at once — looking at latency patterns to separate cause from victims.

causes.reasoning: Central service with immediate stable +2s p99 plateau at 8s while p50 barely moves and its dependencies train/station stay healthy, indicating injected delay that fans out to callers.
Large fluctuating 0.24s to 7.7s p99 jump at same 8s with median also blown up and CPU/requests down, classic victim waiting on slow route.
Huge 0.49s to 19s p99 amplification with median 0.22s to 2.6s, low traffic fan-out service victim of route slowness.
Gradual ramp 0.09s to 1-2.4s over 250s with CPU down, showing queue/backpressure victim rather than immediate fault.
p99 0.09s to 1.1s jump at 14s after route with p50 unchanged and CPU down, tail-only victim pattern downstream of route.
